cards.text: Come on in, friend, we're at Sparkle's station today! Proverbs 15 is a stack of short sayings from Solomon, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1), and a lot of them come in two halves that flip on each other: wise on one side, foolish on the other. The first one is a moment every adult knows: somebody is MAD, and it's your turn to talk.

cards.question: Somebody's angry and you're up next. What does Solomon say a gentle answer does?

cards.text: The other half says a harsh word stirs up anger. One sharp reply, and I have watched a group chat go from "Morning, everybody!" to FORTY-SEVEN unread messages before the oven even finished preheating.
Then Solomon lines up two mouths. The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, and the fool's mouth spouts folly like a garden hose somebody dropped on full blast, flopping around, soaking EVERYBODY.

cards.question: Solomon turns from people's mouths to the LORD. Where does he say the eyes of the LORD are?

cards.text: Every place, observing the evil and the good. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer thinking nobody could see me back there, and it turns out the LORD had eyes on that drawer the whole time, dust and all.

cards.question: In Solomon's picture, a soothing tongue is a tree of life. And a perverse tongue? It can ___ a person's spirit.
Solomon says a fool rejects his father's discipline. And the one who heeds correction? Solomon calls him ___.

cards.text: Then money: the house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble. Picture payday, you open the bank app, and the whole deposit is just TROUBLE.

cards.question: Solomon says the hearts of fools spread knowledge, just like the lips of the wise.

cards.text: Now Solomon sets two things side by side in front of the LORD: the sacrifice of the wicked and the prayer of the upright. Let's see how each one lands with Him, friend.

cards.question: The sacrifice of the wicked or the prayer of the upright. Which one does Solomon say is the LORD's delight?
Solomon says the LORD ___ the way of the wicked, but He ___ those who pursue righteousness.

cards.text: Then a warning: discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path, and he who hates correction will die. That's not a speed bump, friend, that's the end of the road.

cards.question: Solomon says Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD, but the hearts of men stay hidden from Him.

cards.text: A mocker does not love to be reproved, and he won't consult the wise either. That's the guy whose GPS says "Recalculating" forty times in a row, and he STILL won't take the turn.

cards.question: Next, Solomon talks about joy. What does he say a joyful heart makes?

cards.text: Sorrow of the heart, though, crushes the spirit. And while a discerning heart goes looking for knowledge, the fool's mouth just feeds on folly.

cards.question: Solomon says all the days of the oppressed are bad, and he says a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

cards.text: Now Solomon starts lining things up, this one beats that one. First round: "Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil."

cards.question: Solomon keeps going: better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with what?

cards.text: Vegetables with love beat an ox with hatred. Give me ONE plain sugar cookie at a table full of love over a whole TOWER of them in a room where everybody's mad at each other.

cards.question: Solomon says a hot-tempered man stirs up strife, and the man who is slow to anger stirs up even more.

cards.text: Then the slacker: his way is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway. Put a job off long enough and it grows thorns, friend, like the mixing bowl I skipped washing that now has dough GLUED to it since TUESDAY.

cards.question: Solomon says a wise son brings joy to his father, and a foolish man honors his mother.
Solomon says folly is ___ to the one who lacks judgment, while a man of understanding walks a straight path.

cards.text: Then plans: they fail for lack of counsel. I'm the guy who skips the instructions, then stands there holding three extra screws next to a shelf that LEANS.

cards.question: Plans fail for lack of counsel. What does Solomon say happens to plans with many advisers?

cards.text: A man takes joy in a fitting reply, and Solomon adds, "how good is a timely word!" The right words at the right moment hit like a warm cookie fresh off the tray.

cards.question: Solomon says the path of life leads upward for the wise. What does it help the wise man avoid?
Solomon says the LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the ___.

cards.text: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him. He's got the thoughts AND the words covered, friend, so nothing slips past.

cards.question: Solomon says a man greedy for unjust gain brings trouble only on himself, not on his household.

cards.text: Then Solomon puts the righteous and the wicked side by side again. The mouth of the wicked blurts out evil, like a guy hitting Reply All before his brain even finishes loading.

cards.question: The wicked man's mouth blurts out evil. What does Solomon say the heart of the righteous does?
Solomon says the LORD hears the prayer of the righteous, but He is ___ the wicked.

cards.text: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones. And whoever listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.

cards.question: Solomon says whoever heeds correction gains understanding, and whoever ignores discipline is protecting himself.
Solomon wraps up with "The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom," and then a line about honor. What does he say comes before honor?
